The main takeaway from our work is that

the GD dynamics of neural network models is richer than the dynamics associated with the mean-field scaling, and that the GD dynamics can exhibit a quenching- activation process that is reminiscent of that in neural networks, even in the under- and mildly over-parameterized regimes.
the GD dynamics is not simply a random walk in the parameter space but is a highly nontrivial dynamical process that is sensitive to the geometry of the loss surface.

the quenching process provides a mechanism to explain the sparseness and implicit regularization observed in neural network training dynamics, while the mean-field scaling provides a mechanism to understand the over-parameterized regime where the inner-layer weights are effectively frozen.
